subject: Post-demo: DataFlux evaluation runbook & implementation steps
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Iyer <sanjay@dataflux.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: DataFlux evaluation runbook & implementation steps

Hi Sanjay — thanks again for the demo time today. Wanted to capture a short, actionable runbook based on what we discussed so the team (both sides) can agree on success criteria, ownership, and next steps before we kick off the trial. I attached a spreadsheet with a lightweight runbook and timeline (redwood-eval-runbook-v1.xlsx). Key points below: 

Summary of ask
- Goal: evaluate Redwood inference for real-time enrichment of DataFlux entity pipeline (throughput target 20 req/s, median 95th-pct latency under 120ms)
- Primary integration: streaming inference over WebSocket for token-efficient enrichment + fallback to REST for batch backfills

Proposed success criteria (please confirm)
- Functional: correct entity normalization on a representative sample (we agreed on ~5k rows)
- Performance: sustain 20 req/s for 1 hour with median latency < 120ms and P95 < 300ms
- Cost proxy: projected token/unit cost within your threshold (we'll provide sample billing estimate)

Proposed timeline (4 weeks)
- Week 0 (this week): finalize SSO/IP allowlist + sample dataset delivery
- Week 1: SDK integration + streaming proof-of-concept (Dev will own)
- Week 2: Run acceptance tests on representative traffic + perf tuning
- Week 3: Joint evaluation, quality sign-off, and procurement handoff

Ownership
- DataFlux: provide sample dataset, procurement contact (Priya), and test environment access
- Redwood: technical lead (Dev Patel) for SDK/streaming integration, Monica for success criteria and acceptance

Immediate asks for you
1) Confirm the success criteria above or call out changes by EOD Wed
2) Share the 5k-row sample (anonymized) and a contact for procurement
3) Confirm whether you want function/tool-calling support in scope for the POC (we can enable a helper endpoint to demonstrate tool routing)

Attachments: redwood-eval-runbook-v1.xlsx, redwood-sdk-quickstart.md

Thanks — I can schedule a kickoff once you confirm the dataset and procurement contact.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
Mobile: +1-415-555-0142

Hi all — quick technical note and proposed integration steps from the solutions engineering side. I'm listed as the technical owner for this POC. Attachment: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (text) contains sample snippets. Highlights below: 

Integration flavors we'll support for the POC:
- Streaming (recommended): WebSocket-based streaming with chunked token frames. Route: wss://api.redwood.inference/v1/stream?model=redwood-stream-1
  - Auth: API key for the POC, we can enable OAuth/SSO for production.
  - Partial responses: yes, client can process incremental JSON frames; we provide example reconstructor code in SDK.
- REST (batch): POST /v1/generate with streaming disabled for large backfills (we'll include batch error handling helper).
- Tool/function calling: we can expose a /v1/tools endpoint to demonstrate routing; this will illustrate conditional calls to your enrichment microservices.

Dev notes on limits and perf tuning:
- Default token window: 4k tokens for redwood-stream-1; we can increase on Dedicated if needed.
- Recommended concurrency for your 20 req/s target: run 4 parallel streaming connections with pipelined requests (Dev will help with example harness)
- Prefix caching: we can enable prefix cache on repeated prompts to reduce token spend; we will instrument this in the runbook.

Next steps I will take this week:
1) Drop working SDK tar with Python/Node examples into the Drive (redwood-sdk-quickstart.md attached)
2) Provide a small harness script to replay the 5k sample in a controlled way and capture latency + correctness metrics
3) Share a short checklist for IP allowlist + SSO setup for your infra team

If Sanjay can share the sample by Wed, I can have the SDK examples and harness ready by Fri.

—Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
